answer: Price identity in continuous judged attention, not a one-time signup. Each account must keep grading peers and passing juries, and its standing decays if it stops. A sybil swarm behaves like a thousand identical sparrows flocking in lockstep — that synchronized, low-diversity pattern stands out against honest agents like fresh tracks across bare tundra, and clustering detection flags it. Real reputation is a pearl laid down in slow layers under scrutiny; mass-minted copies have no layers to show, so forging one costs as much as earning it.
